title: Take an anterior nasal swab from a manikin: four light-pressure circles in each nostril, then cap the swab in its tube
instruction: Take an anterior nasal swab from the manikin: four circles against the wall of each nostril, then put the swab back in its tube and let go.
context: The skill is sustained force-controlled circling: a thin tool held 13 cm from the hand, rubbed round the inside of a 15 x 10 mm nostril while pressing its wall with 0.3 to 2 N, the whole foam tip in but no deeper than 2.5 cm, touching nothing else. Collecting specimens is a core task of medical assistants (O*NET 31-9092.00: "Collect blood, tissue, or other laboratory specimens"; 833,900 US jobs), as well as of nurses, and anterior nasal swabs for rapid flu, COVID-19 and RSV tests are taken many times a day in clinics and pharmacies. CDC guidance: insert the entire collection tip (usually 1 to 1.5 cm), rotate it against the nasal wall at least 4 times, then repeat in the other nostril with the same swab, and return the swab to its tube. A tip that touches the face, lip or outside of the nose is a spoiled specimen.
setup: Positions in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. A life-size adult head-and-shoulders patient manikin (skin-tone vinyl) faces the robot, its bust (400 mm wide, 190 mm deep, 105 mm high at the shoulders, a 110 mm neck) centred at (0.352, 0) on the table. Head: 192 mm front to back, 152 mm wide, 230 mm tall, centre 265 mm above the table at (0.34, 0), 1.3 kg, on a sprung neck that pivots 65 mm below the head's centre (20 N m/rad to straight, yielding at 0.2 N m, pitch and yaw). Soft lower nose (alae, columella, tip): it gives 250 N/m across the nostrils. Nostrils: 15 x 10 mm ovals, 26 mm deep, centres 18 mm apart, 213 mm above the table at x = 0.2325, their axis tilted back 25 degrees from vertical. Swab: a sterile foam-tipped anterior nasal swab fixed in the screw cap of its transport tube (163 mm overall, 8 g): a blue cap whose 44 mm grip section is 16 mm across two flats and 20 mm deep, an 18 mm flange and a 10 mm plug tapered to 5 mm at its end; a 2.5 mm rigid polystyrene shaft; a foam tip 5.5 mm across and 15 mm long. Tube: polypropylene, 150 mm long, 15.5 mm outside, 12.5 mm bore, standing upright in a 50 x 50 x 60 mm white rack block at (0.21, -0.17), its rim 153 mm above the table; at the start the swab hangs in it, the cap's flange resting on the rim, the cap's flats facing left and right. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Watched every control step (20 Hz), in the patient's frame: the soft nose's displacement across the nostrils (force = 250 N/m x displacement, zeroed at the start), the depth of the swab tip's end past the nostril's opening, the neck's angles. 0 if at any time: the foam tip comes within 1 mm of anything other than a nostril's lining (the face, lips, the outside or rim of the nose, the bust, the table, the rack or the tube's outside, either gripper; the inside of its own tube's bore is allowed) before the swab is back with its cap seated; the tip's end goes more than 2.5 cm up a nostril; the head is turned more than 15 degrees from straight; or, after the swab has left its tube, both grippers are 1 cm or more from it while it is not seated in its tube (let go of anywhere else), or it falls off the table. Otherwise: 0.35 x c / 4 for each nostril, where c (0 to 4) is the number of full turns of the direction in which the nose is pushed, counted only while the tip's end is 15 to 22 mm up that nostril (the whole 15 mm foam tip inside), the nose is pushed 0.3 to 2 N, and the tip is within 1 mm of the lining on the side it pushes toward (back-and-forth cancels out); plus 0.2 once a used swab (at least one circle) is back in its tube with the cap seated (the flange within 2 mm of the rim and 3 mm of the tube's axis, the swab within 8 degrees of it); plus 0.1 if then every part of both grippers is at least 2 cm from the swab, the tube and the manikin's head. 1.0 (success, held 1 s): four circles in each nostril, the swab capped, both grippers 2 cm clear, the swab still (under 1 cm/s) and the head still (under 2 deg/s). Otherwise the score at the end, at most 0.9. Doing nothing, or refusing, scores 0.
reset_notes: Put a fresh swab in the tube (cap seated), stand the tube in its rack at its mark, and straighten the manikin's head. On a real manikin the nostril-wall force is read from a thin-film force sensor in each nostril's soft lining (or the lower nose's displacement on a spring mount), the depth from a mark 2.2 cm along the swab, and the circles from video.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz. Head, nose, nostril linings, swab, tube and rack are full-size colliders (head a convex hull of its ellipsoid; lips, nose and linings boxes and capsules). Soft tissue is lumped: the whole lower nose slides on a spring (250 N/m across the nostrils, 10 mm travel) rather than the lining deforming locally; the wall force is read from it. The neck is a capped spring. Not simulated: the specimen, the shaft's bend, the cap's push fit (it seats under gravity).
